descriptionChirho: A wheeled war vehicle or the collective chariot force of an army — the dominant sense covering single chariots, chariot fleets, and chariot corps, confirmed by Arabic مَرْكَبَة/مَرْكَبَات, Korean 병거/전차, and Swahili magari ya vita across all grammatical inflections.

The upper grinding stone of a hand-mill — a metaphorical extension from the root r-k-b 'to ride,' as the upper stone 'rides' atop the lower, confirmed by Arabic رَحًى (millstone), Korean 맷돌/윗돌 (millstone/upper-stone), and Swahili jiwe la kusagia/jiwe la juu (grinding stone/upper stone).
